title: Path provenance rollup with cost-aware sampling
creator: Ava Chen
description: Proposal and implementation plan to introduce a compact path-provenance rollup and a cost-aware hybrid sampling scheme for routing decisions. Goal: improve troubleshooting and RCA for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants while bounding telemetry storage costs and minimizing per-request overhead. Deliver a trace/event schema, server and agent instrumentation changes, an ingestion pipeline with delta/rollup encoding, dashboards, and alerting rules.
acceptance_criteria: New decision_trace event schema accepted and deployed to canary (hosted) with backward-compatible fields
Hybrid sampling toggles implemented: 100% for P0 customers, adaptive probabilistic for others with config knob per-route
Compact rollup format reduces average stored payload size by >= 70% vs naive full trace for sampled flows
End-to-end pipeline writes sampled full traces to long-retention archive (BigQuery) and rollups to ClickHouse/OLAP for dashboards
Dashboard shows per-route model variant hit-rate, region selection latency breakdown, and fallback frequency with 5m rollups
Instrumentation overhead measured: mean added latency < 2ms per request and <= 1% increased p50 latency budget consumption
Security review completed with PII redaction and hashed customer identifiers for traces
tasks: Design event schema (decision_trace, hop_record, rollup_summary) and publish Confluence spec
Add trace_id and hop_id propagation to routing decision path in runtime (C++/Go)
Implement client-side lightweight sampling control header and server-side sampling decision service
Develop delta-encoding library for hop enrichment (proto->compact json) and integrate into ingestion
Build streaming job: consume raw events from Kafka, produce full-traces to archive topic and rollups to OLAP topic
Create Console dashboards: per-route routing provenance, fallback triggers, region selection heatmap
Add alerting: fallback-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, model_variant_mismatch anomalies
End-to-end perf test with synthetic traffic to validate overhead and storage estimates
Rollout plan and feature flag for gradual enablement by customer tier
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Telemetry, and Console teams. Agreed on goals and cost constraints.
2026-02-26: Initial schema draft posted to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/routing-provenance-v1 (internal)
2026-03-03: Runtime PR created to propagate trace_id/hop_id and attach policy_version (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4321)
2026-03-05: Security review flagged raw user_id in traces. Decided to replace user_id with hashed_user and to redact prompt text by default.
2026-03-08: Prototype delta-encoder implemented in Rust; size reduction benchmarks show ~78% median payload reduction for long multi-hop traces.
2026-03-12: Streaming consumer job topology reviewed with Data Eng. ClickHouse schema for rollups agreed; retention/cost estimates updated. Preparing canary deploy for hosted region-us-east-1.
decisions: Use hybrid sampling: forced sampling at 100% for P0/enterprise customers and 1% baseline for self-serve with adaptive ramping based on anomaly signals
Adopt delta-encoded hop enrichment: store full first-hop and then incremental diffs for subsequent hops to enable compact rollups
Two-tier storage model: sampled full traces -> long-retention archive (BigQuery), compact rollups -> ClickHouse for fast queries and dashboards

Redact prompt text and replace customer identifiers with hashed_user to satisfy compliance. Full unredacted traces can be enabled only with legal-approved retention for enterprise customers behind Flag and KMS protections
Expose a per-route sampling override API for SRE and Support to force-sample flows for live investigations
risks: Telemetry volume could still exceed budget if fallback storms occur across many customers; mitigated by cost-aware downsampling and dynamic backpressure
Incorrect delta-encoding could make rollups difficult to interpret for humans; will provide server-side denormalizer in Console for investigator UX
Privacy exposure if redaction/hashing misapplied; Security requires automated tests and monthly audit of stored traces
Runtime changes might add contention points on critical path; plan to keep enrichment asynchronous and rely on sampling decisions to bound overhead
dependencies: ENG-20844: kafka-topology-upgrades (data platform capacity for new topics)
PM-145: console-routing-dashboards (Console team to add visualization components)
SEC-34: telemetry-pii-policy (security approval for hashed identifiers and retention)
notes: Operational knobs: per-route sampling weight, anomaly-triggered immediate sampling, customer-tier overrides
Rollup schema will include: trace_id, route, policy_version, model_variant, region, hop_count, total_tokens, latency_ms, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, fallback_reason (if any), sample_weight
Investigators will be able to request full-trace rehydration (server-side) for sampled rollups, gated by flag and audit log
We will add unit and integration tests that validate schema forward/backwards compatibility and performance budgets
